001_N: ["You walk up to the school gate, and the new guard holds up a hand.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
004_N: ["There's grey in your hair, your knees click on the stairs, and your phone just buzzed with your weekly screen time report.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
006_N: ["So what if every hour on your phone aged you one day?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
007_N: ["Not your battery. Not your eyes. Your whole body. One hour on a screen, one day older.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
008_N: ["And it only counts the screen in your own hands. Remember that. It matters later.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
009_N: ["Let's go back to where it started. Your sixteenth birthday.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
010_N: ["That night you scroll in bed until three in the morning. Five hours. Dance videos, memes, a man pressure-washing a driveway.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
011_N: ["In the morning, the number floating over your head says sixteen years and five days.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
012_N: ["You figure it's a glitch. Then you spend the weekend gaming with your best friend Kai. Twenty hours.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
013_N: ["Monday, you have stubble. Real stubble. At sixteen.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
014_N: ["Kai is on his phone just as much as you, and Kai still looks twelve.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
015_N: ["So you test it. Kai holds your phone and reads every message out loud. The number doesn't move.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
016_N: ["Rule one: one hour on a screen, one day on your body. Rule two: only the screen in your hands counts.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
017_N: ["Now the math. American teenagers average about eight and a half hours of screen entertainment a day.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
018_N: ["That's eight and a half days of aging, every single day. Almost nine years for every year you live.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
019_N: ["At your pace, you graduate at thirty-six. By twenty-one, you'd get the senior discount.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
020_N: ["And honestly? The first few months are kind of great.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
021_N: ["Nobody asks for your ID at the movies. The bank calls you sir. A waiter hands your mom the kids' menu and hands you the wine list.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
023_N: ["At seventeen, your back hurts when you sneeze. You make a noise every time you stand up. You say back in my day about last Tuesday.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
024_N: ["And the phone keeps calling you back. A typical teen gets around two hundred and thirty notifications a day.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
025_N: ["Two hundred and thirty little taps on the shoulder. Each one says, just one minute. It is never one minute.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
026_N: ["You try to quit. Day one, your hand keeps reaching for a phone that isn't there.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
027_N: ["Your pocket buzzes, and nothing is in it. In one study, eighty-nine percent of college students said they felt phantom vibrations like that.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
028_N: ["Day two, you find your old handheld console, just to check the battery. Four hours. Four days.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
029_N: ["So you make Kai your human phone. He reads your messages, scrolls your feed, and narrates your videos.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
030_N: ["Okay, a cat falls off a table. Now it's angry. Now it's... eating?",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
032_N: ["Then Kai gets tired of being your phone. And you get tired of hearing the whole internet in Kai's voice.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
033_N: ["The group chat moves on without you. Plans get made at midnight, and you find out at noon.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
034_N: ["Nora invites everyone to the lake. Everyone except the guy who looks like a substitute teacher.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
035_N: ["At seventeen and a half, you're thirty-one. The mirror is the worst app you own.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
036_N: ["So you get on a bus to the one person in your family who never owned a smartphone. Grandma Rosa.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
037_N: ["Grandma Rosa lives two hours out of town, with a garden, a chess board, and a phone that flips.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
038_N: ["She looks at your grey hair, doesn't ask a single question, and hands you a shovel.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
039_N: ["Here's what science says happened to the rest of us. Psychologist Gloria Mark measured how long people focus on one screen before switching.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
040_N: ["Around two thousand four, it was about two and a half minutes. Today, it's about forty-seven seconds.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
041_N: ["At Grandma's house, there's nothing to switch to. So you dig. You cook. You lose at chess. Eleven times.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
042_N: ["And somewhere in week two, you notice it. The number over your head hasn't moved in nine days.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
043_N: ["That night, by the fire, Grandma tells you why she never bought a smartphone.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
044_N: ["In nineteen seventy-two, she says, every hour of television made her one day older.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
046_N: ["It runs in the family. She switched off the only screen she had, and never looked back.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
047_N: ["Those days don't come back, she says. But the ones you live with your eyes up are the only ones that feel long.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
048_N: ["Then winter comes. One Saturday, Grandma walks up the ridge trail to fix a fence, the way she has for forty years.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
049_N: ["At four o'clock, a storm rolls in. At five, she isn't back. Her flip phone goes straight to voicemail.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
050_N: ["The rescue team is two hours away. The trail splits into six paths, and the snow is erasing her footprints.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
051_N: ["There's one thing that can find her. A screen. A map, her last signal, the weather radar.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
052_N: ["You don't care about the days it will cost. The problem is your hands. You need them for the flashlight, the rope, and her.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
053_N: ["And then you remember rule two. Only the screen in your hands counts.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
054_N: ["You call Kai. It's been a month. He answers anyway.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
055_N: ["Kai becomes your eyes. He watches the radar from his room and talks you up the mountain, turn by turn.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
056_N: ["Left at the broken pine. Two hundred steps. Her phone last pinged near the creek.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
057_N: ["Your knees are thirty-one and they're screaming. But your eyes are up, and you see what a screen would never show you. One red glove in the snow.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
058_N: ["She's under a rock ledge, ankle twisted, absolutely furious at the fence.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
059_N: ["You carry her down. Kai guides the rescue team to the trailhead. Nobody looks at a single number all night.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
060_N: ["In the morning, the number over your head says thirty-one years and two days. Two days for that trip. Worth it.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
061_N: ["Here's the real part. Your phone can't age your face.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
062_N: ["But the average American spends around four and a half hours a day on their phone.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
063_N: ["From age ten to eighty, that's about thirteen years of your life. Awake. Looking down.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
064_N: ["Nobody gives those years back. You just get to choose what the next ones look like.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
065_N: ["So you keep the phone. You just stop letting it hold you.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
066_N: ["On Monday, you walk up to the school gate. The guard holds up a hand.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
068_N: ["You grin. Not today. Today I've got a class to catch up on.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
069_N: ["So tell me. What did your screen time say yesterday? Be honest. And yes, you're watching this on a phone.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
070_N: ["Subscribe. It takes one second. That's not even a day.",{"fish":"0327fdb5da9e4fd782899a8058c8ae2b"}]
